questions.prompt: A logging listener on a waterfall hook forgets to call next() and returns undefined. What happens to the real action?
options: It runs anyway after the listener returns
It never runs, for every caller, because the layers inside the listener are skipped
questions.explanation: Not calling next is how a listener decides alone. A logger that forgets it blocks the action and every listener inside it.

questions.prompt: timer is the outer listener and blocker the inner one. A delete_file call is blocked. Does timer print a time?
options: No, because the tool never ran
No, because blocker throws an error
Yes, because timer wraps blocker and gets blocker's return value from next()
Only if the tool runs longer than 30 seconds
questions.explanation: timer calls next(), which runs blocker. blocker returns the error text, so next() resolves and timer prints how long that took.

questions.prompt: Why does the waterfall throw when a listener calls next() a second time?
options: Because a second call would run the wrapped action twice
Because next() can only return a string
Because listeners may only run once per program
Because the listener list is emptied after the first call
questions.explanation: Each next() runs every inner layer and then the action itself. Allowing two calls would, for example, run a tool twice.
